baking: 1 hour|difficulty=3|image=[[Image:23-pies finished.jpg|300px]] }} __NOTOC__ {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]] This recipe makes enough dough for one 23 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] (9 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) covered pie. If your pie only requires a bottom crust, use half this recipe. However, for best results, make the full recipe. If only a single crust is required, make the full recipe and freeze half for later. In contrast to [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], pie crust and other pastries should be made in a way that minimizes the development of [[Cookbook:Gluten|gluten]]. Once the water has been added, the dough should be worked as little as possible to minimize toughness in the finished crust. == Ingredients == * 310 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] * 6 g (1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 4 g (1 tsp) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] (optional) * 225 g (1 cup) cold [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] * 95 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (⅓ cup + 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) cold water == Procedure == # [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] flour, salt and sugar together in a deep bowl. # Cut the butter into small pieces and add to the flour mixture. # Using a [[Cookbook:Pastry Blender|pastry blender]] or two butter knives, cut the butter into the flour until the butter is in small pea-sized pieces. # Add cold water; cut the water into the flour-butter mixture with the edge of a rubber [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]] until it is evenly moistened and will hold together when pressed. # Form the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] into a ball with your hands, kneading in any loose flour. This should be done as quickly as possible to avoid melting the butter in the dough. # Chill the dough for 10–20 minutes. # Cut the dough evenly in half. # On a lightly floured board, roll each half out until it will cover a 20 cm (9 inch) [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie dish]], with about 2 cm (¾" inch) overhang. File:07-crust dry ingredients.jpg|Dry ingredients File:08-crust butter.jpg|Added butter File:09-crust blended.jpg|Blended butter File:10-crust with water.jpg|With added water File:11-crust balled.jpg|Dough rolled into a ball File:12-crust on board.jpg|Dough on a lightly floured board File:13-crust flattened.jpg|Dough flattened File:14-crust rolled.jpg|Dough rolled out File:15-crust size.jpg|Rolled dough compared to pie dish File:16-crust in dish.jpg|Crust in pie dish === Shaping === # Lay the bottom crust in the pie dish, ensuring that there are no gaps between the crust and the bottom of the dish. # Fill the crust with the pie filling. # Place the top crust on top, leaving equal overhang on all sides. # Cut the overhang to about 2 cm (¾" inch) all around the pie. # Working around the pie, hold the bottom and top crust overhangs together and tuck the combined overhang into the pie dish behind the bottom crust. # With the forefinger and thumb of each hand, pinch the ridge formed by the tuck into a decorative edge, or press this ridge with a fork. # Brush the top of the pie with milk, and sprinkle with sugar. # Cut vents in the top crust so that steam can escape. # For a fruit pie, bake on the lower-middle rack of an oven at 220 °C (425 °F) for 30 minutes to set the crust, then at 180 °C (350 °F) for 30 minutes to cook the filling. File:17-crust filled.jpg|Crust filled with fruit File:18-pie covered.jpg|Top crust laid over filled bottom crust File:19-pie edge.jpg|2 cm overhang File:20-pie edge fold.jpg|How crust is folded over File:21-pie folded.jpg|Edge completely folded over File:22-pie crimped.jpg|Edge of crust decoratively crimped File:23-pies finished.jpg|Finished pies File:24-pie milk sugar detail.jpg|Milk brushed on top crust and sprinkled with sugar File:25-pie ventholes.jpg|Vents cut in top crust File:26-pies in oven.jpg|Pies in the oven ==Notes, tips, and variations== * '''Vegan crust:''' Use a [[Cookbook:Vegan_Substitutions|hard vegan fat]], such as [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] in place of the butter (used for the images shown above) * '''Traditional crust:''' Use [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]], which is less saturated than butter and produces the flakiest crusts. * '''Top Crust Colouring:''' Brush on lightly beaten egg white to colour crust instead of milk. * When baking two pies at once, rotate the pies 180 degrees at 15 minutes and 45 minutes of baking to ensure the crust does not burn due to its proximity to the oven walls. steps.text: Whisk flour, salt and sugar together in a deep bowl.
Cut the butter into small pieces and add to the flour mixture.
Using a pastry blender or two butter knives, cut the butter into the flour until the butter is in small pea-sized pieces.
Add cold water; cut the water into the flour-butter mixture with the edge of a rubber spatula until it is evenly moistened and will hold together when pressed.
Form the dough into a ball with your hands, kneading in any loose flour. This should be done as quickly as possible to avoid melting the butter in the dough.
Chill the dough for 10–20 minutes.
Cut the dough evenly in half.
On a lightly floured board, roll each half out until it will cover a 20 cm (9 inch) pie dish, with about 2 cm (¾" inch) overhang.
Lay the bottom crust in the pie dish, ensuring that there are no gaps between the crust and the bottom of the dish.
Fill the crust with the pie filling.
Place the top crust on top, leaving equal overhang on all sides.
Cut the overhang to about 2 cm (¾" inch) all around the pie.
Working around the pie, hold the bottom and top crust overhangs together and tuck the combined overhang into the pie dish behind the bottom crust.
With the forefinger and thumb of each hand, pinch the ridge formed by the tuck into a decorative edge, or press this ridge with a fork.
Brush the top of the pie with milk, and sprinkle with sugar.
Cut vents in the top crust so that steam can escape.
For a fruit pie, bake on the lower-middle rack of an oven at 220 °C (425 °F) for 30 minutes to set the crust, then at 180 °C (350 °F) for 30 minutes to cook the filling.
